key_insight: Embedding an asymptotic boundary-layer corrector in neural trial functions preserves accuracy as viscosity decreases, without requiring a grid that resolves the thin vorticity layer.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables coarse-grid neural solutions of small-viscosity flow problems, with a finite-volume variant costing about half as much per training step.
method: Use the vorticity–stream function formulation of 2D incompressible flow with slip boundary conditions.
Embed the asymptotic layer profile and tie its amplitude to the network’s wall trace, avoiding prior knowledge of the limit solution.
Replace the residual’s Laplacian evaluation with coarse-grid finite-volume flux differences in sl-FVNN.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports viscosity-uniform accuracy across six decades for Stokes and Navier–Stokes tests, with sl-FVNN matching sl-PINN within random-seed scatter.
watch_item: The reported results concern 2D flows with slip boundaries; extension to other boundary conditions requires appropriate correctors and validation.
paper_title: Singular layer neural networks for the Navier-Stokes equations at small viscosity
